description: Pre-seeded demo workspace for advisorprephero.com/try (financial advisor pack — the default). A fictional advisory household (the Webbs) so the demo shows the confidential-client-work story for an RIA / wealth manager, not founder content. The client folder holds realistic files the way an advisor actually keeps them: Word documents (the plan, the meeting notes) and PDFs (a custodian beneficiary record, a client intake), NOT markdown. Word docs are generated from each file's `content` at seed time; PDFs are pre-built committed assets in ./sample-docs (regenerate with `node scripts/build-demo-pdfs.mjs`). The plain-text `content` here is also what the demo's Ask retriever indexes and cites, so it must stay in sync with the binary. All names, numbers, and facts are invented for illustration. Bump version to re-seed.

# You're inside a real Advisor Prep Hero workspace

This whole thing is running in your browser. No install, no account, nothing saved to a server. It's a pretend client household for a financial advisor, pre-loaded so you can actually poke around instead of staring at an empty screen.

Everything here is a real Advisor Prep Hero surface. The files are real files — Word documents and PDFs, the way they'd live on your own machine. The editor is the real editor. The AI sidebar talks to a real model.

## What to try

1. Start on the **Client Map** you're looking at. It's the one-screen picture of this household that Advisor Prep Hero built from the files, and every line links back to the document it came from. Look at the stale beneficiary on the old 401(k) — click that line's source chip and it opens the actual custodian PDF where the problem lives.
2. Open the files in **Webb Household**: the financial plan and the meeting notes are Word documents; the beneficiary record and the intake are PDFs — exactly what you'd have for a real client.
3. Open **Ask** and ask a question about the household. Every answer cites the file it came from, and you can click the citation to land on that file. Ask it something the files don't cover and watch it say so instead of making something up — that's deliberate.
4. Hit a limit? Paste your own Anthropic key for unlimited use, or download the app.

Here's the part that matters. On your own machine, these files live in a folder you pick, and your API key goes straight from your computer to the model. Nothing routes through a server I control. That's the whole point of Advisor Prep Hero, and it's why an advisor can use it on real client data.

Refresh the page and the workspace comes back to where it started.

# Financial Plan Summary: Webb Household

**Clients:** Marcus Webb (38) and Tanya Webb (37)

**Dependents:** Caleb (8), Ava (5)

**Goals:** Retire at 60, fund both kids' college, pay off the house early

**Risk profile:** Moderate growth (completed questionnaire, March 2026)

## Where things stand

- **Marcus 401(k):** $412,000, contributing 12% plus a 4% match. Old employer 401(k) of $96,000 still sitting at the prior custodian, not yet rolled over.
- **Tanya 403(b):** $188,000, contributing 9%.
- **Joint brokerage:** $145,000, mostly index funds.
- **Roth IRAs:** $61,000 (Marcus), $54,000 (Tanya).
- **529 plans:** $48,000 (Caleb), $29,000 (Ava).
- **Cash reserve:** $55,000 (about 5 months of expenses).
- **Mortgage:** $318,000 at 5.1%, 26 years left.

## The plan, in one paragraph

Roll the old 401(k) into Marcus's IRA so it's managed alongside everything else. Keep both kids' 529s on the current monthly auto-contribution. Revisit a Roth conversion in a low-income year. Hold the moderate-growth allocation; rebalance once a year. Do not pay down the mortgage faster yet, the retirement runway matters more right now.

## Open items

- Confirm the rollover paperwork and the receiving account.
- Recheck beneficiary designations across every account (see the beneficiary record).
- Decide on the Roth conversion amount before year-end.
- Top up the 529 plans before December for the state tax deduction.

# Review Notes: Webb Household

**Meeting:** Annual review

**Date:** June 12, 2026

**Present:** Marcus and Tanya Webb, me

Rough notes taken during the review. Clean up and file the action items.

## What they told me

- Marcus changed jobs last year. The $96k from the old employer 401(k) is still at the prior custodian. He wants it "in one place."
- They want to talk through the 401(k) rollover and Caleb's 529 (his words from the email).
- Tanya got a raise. They can push another $400/month into savings.
- They are nervous about the market and asked, again, whether they should move to cash. Walked them through the moderate-growth plan and the time horizon. They felt better.
- Marcus mentioned, almost in passing, that he and his first wife divorced in 2019 and he "updated everything." Worth verifying.

## What we agreed to do

- Roll the old 401(k) into Marcus's IRA. I'll start the paperwork.
- Increase the joint brokerage auto-contribution by $400/month.
- Revisit the Roth conversion before December.
- Recheck every beneficiary designation. Marcus's comment about the divorce is exactly why.

## My flags

- The old 401(k) rollover is the priority, it's been sitting too long.
- Verify beneficiaries personally. "I updated everything" after a divorce is the single most common place a household has a stale form. Do not take it on faith.
- Next review booked for the fall.

Beneficiary Designation Record — Meridian Trust & Custody

Marcus & Tanya Webb. Consolidated across custodians. Confirm each row against the custodian's record of record; do not rely on client recollection. Relationship opened September 4, 2025.

Beneficiary designations on file:

401(k) (current employer) | Marcus | Tanya Webb (100%) | Caleb & Ava (50/50) | last confirmed Jan 2026

Old 401(k) (prior employer) | Marcus | Jessica Reyes (100%) | None listed | dated 2019

403(b) | Tanya | Marcus Webb (100%) | Caleb & Ava (50/50) | last confirmed Jan 2026

Roth IRA | Marcus | Tanya Webb (100%) | Caleb & Ava (50/50) | last confirmed Jan 2026

Roth IRA | Tanya | Marcus Webb (100%) | Caleb & Ava (50/50) | last confirmed Jan 2026

Joint brokerage (TOD) | Marcus & Tanya | each other | Caleb & Ava (50/50) | last confirmed Jan 2026

Flag — Old 401(k), prior employer. This account still lists Jessica Reyes, Marcus's first wife, as the sole primary beneficiary, dated 2019, with no contingent listed. Marcus believes he "updated everything" after the divorce. This designation was not updated. If he died before the rollover, that account (approximately $96,000) would pass to his ex-spouse, not to Tanya.

This is the reason the rollover matters beyond convenience: rolling the account into Marcus's IRA places it under the IRA's correct beneficiaries. Confirm every row against the custodian, not the client's memory.

Statement of record only. Not tax or legal advice. Beneficiary designations supersede instructions in a will for the listed accounts.

Client Intake Summary — Lakebourne Wealth Advisors (fee-only financial planning)

Household: Marcus & Tanya Webb. Married, two minor children: Caleb (8), Ava (5). Date opened: September 4, 2025. Engagement: comprehensive financial planning plus ongoing investment management.

What the clients want: retire by 60, get both kids through college without loans, and stop worrying every time the market dips. They want one place that sees the whole picture instead of five logins. Goal: retire by 60. Get both kids through college without loans. Pay off the house early.

Came in wary after a prior advisor missed a beneficiary issue; wants someone who catches what they would miss.

Accounts under advisement: Marcus 401(k), Marcus old 401(k) (rollover pending), Tanya 403(b), two Roth IRAs, joint brokerage, two 529 plans. Mortgage and cash reserve tracked but not managed.

Key facts to verify: beneficiary designation on the old 401(k) (see the beneficiary designations record); the receiving account and paperwork for the rollover; current contribution rates after Tanya's raise.

Note: this is a planning record, not tax or legal advice. Coordinate the Roth conversion timing with their CPA before executing. No estate attorney on file.

# About this demo

This is the in-browser version of Advisor Prep Hero. It runs the same editor, file tree, and AI chat the desktop app uses, just pre-loaded with a fictional client household so you have something to look at.

The household, the names, and the numbers are all made up for illustration. Nothing here is financial advice, and the AI's job in the real app is to produce a first draft you review, not to make recommendations on its own.

What's different from the real app: this demo uses a shared, rate-limited key so you can try the AI without setting anything up. On your own machine you bring your own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or a local model through Ollama), and your files and your key never leave your computer.

When you're ready, download the 30-day trial at advisorprephero.com.
